title: Session Reservoir PRD: Quant-aware Warmup and Eviction
author: Aisha Morales
body:
Overview:

This PRD proposes the Session Reservoir: a productized subsystem that improves per-tenant throughput, cold-start latency, and cost efficiency by managing an adaptive pool of warmed session state (KV cache, quantized weights, and warm execution context) across hosted and dedicated runtimes. The feature combines quantization-awareness, predictive warmup, and eviction policies to keep hot sessions fast while bounding memory/GPU overhead and minimizing cross-tenant interference.

Why this matters:
- Customers frequently see the worst latency and cost on first requests after idle periods (cold-starts) or model variant fallbacks.
- Existing sticky-session approaches reserve capacity inefficiently or require manual rules per-customer.
- A transparent reservoir that is SLO-aligned and cost-aware enables predictable economics for hosted tier and smoother migrations to Dedicated/Private.

Goals (measurable):
1. Reduce median P50 generation latency for warmup-sensitive workloads by >= 22% for customers with session-oriented traffic within 90 days of launch (measured on representative sample tenants).
2. Reduce cold-call token generation P95 latency by >= 35% for affected routes where reservoir warmup applies.
3. Keep additional GPU memory footprint per node below 6% on average after warm pool stabilization for Dedicated pools.
4. Avoid >0.5% increase in cross-tenant request failures attributable to reservoir operations.
5. Provide consumption visibility and per-tenant costs for warmup operations in Console (cost line-item).

Non-goals:
- This PRD does not replace full model preloading for Dedicated reserved deployments (that remains a separate offering).
- Not intended to manage data residency or encryption changes; sessions will respect existing KMS and tenancy controls.

Scope (MVP):
- Predictor service components: warmup scheduler, quant-aware serializer, in-memory reservoir manager, and eviction controller.
- Console: per-route toggle, dashboard telemetry (warm hits, warms/sec, eviction rate, memory delta), and cost attribution.
- API: new per-request headers to declare session affinity hints and an admin API to query / control warm state per-tenant.
- Telemetry & billing hooks for warm operations (consumable in Optimize and Console).

MVP Requirements (priority ordered):
1. Reservoir lifecycle: create reservoir entries when affinity hints indicate a new session; store KV cache snapshot + lightweight execution state identifier + quantization descriptor (Q-profile id).
2. Quant-aware warmup: when warming, apply a "best-fit" quantization profile based on tenant fidelity budget and route fidelity preference (profiles: q4_0, q4_1, q8_0) and keep descriptor with the reservoir entry.
3. Predictive warm scheduler: maintain a moving-window usage model per-route (30m/6h/24h) and proactively warm entries for high-probability sessions up to configurable tenant thresholds.
4. Eviction policy: hybrid LRU + cost-shield policy that prioritizes evicting entries by lowest expected future benefit per GB and respects tenant soft-limits; provide emergency global-evict step if total memory delta exceeds node threshold (default 8%).
5. SLO alignment: reservoir operations must not delay on-path requests; warm operations are background and must preempt only within configured IO/cpu budgets; fallbacks must still produce result within original route SLOs.
6. Visibility: surface warm hit/miss, average warm time, memory delta per-node and per-tenant, and a per-tenant warm cost estimate in Console & telemetry.

API & Console (example snippets):
- Request header example (client sets affinity hint):

  X-Redwood-Session-Affinity: "session-id=tenant123:user456;hint=conversational;ttl=600"

- Admin API (GET warm state for tenant):

  GET /admin/v1/warmstate?tenant=tenant123
  Response (example):
  {
    "tenant": "tenant123",
    "entries": 12,
    "memory_delta_bytes": 12_345_678,
    "recent_evictions": 3
  }

Note: admin API payloads above are illustrative — final schema will be defined in the API contract doc.

Design considerations and tradeoffs:
- Quantization choice vs. fidelity: warmer quant profiles reduce warm times and memory, but can degrade output quality. We include a per-tenant fidelity budget used by the Quant Advisor to select a profile that minimizes quality regression while saving memory/cost.
- Memory fragmentation across GPU devices: reservoir entries should be co-located with existing session allocations where possible to avoid cross-device copies; colocated warm pools per-AZ are preferred.
- Multi-tenant fairness: the eviction policy must be conservative to avoid tenant eviction storms during bursts; introduce a short-term fairness window that penalizes repeated evictions for same tenant.

Telemetry and Metrics (to emit):
- warm_request_count (per-route, per-tenant)
- warm_success_count, warm_failure_count
- warm_hit_ratio (per-route, per-minute)
- avg_warm_time_ms, p95_warm_time_ms
- memory_delta_bytes_per_node, reservoir_size_entries
- eviction_rate_per_minute, eviction_reason_{cost,age,global}
- warm_cost_estimate_cents_per_hour (per-tenant)

Success criteria (90 days post-launch):
- Meets goals for latency reductions on 70% of sampled tenants with session-like traffic;
- Warm hit ratio > 60% for routes enabled by default rules;
- No customer-facing incidents attributed to reservoir operations;
- Billing visibility adopted by at least 25% of tenants who enabled reservoir in Console.

Rollout plan and phases:
1. Canary (2 weeks): internal canary tenants + Redwood SRE test tenants. Validate stability under controlled synthetic traffic, verify memory delta guardrails.
2. Early Access (6 weeks): invite customers (hosted) with session traffic patterns categorized as "chatty". Collect qualitative feedback and fidelity regressions with shadow evaluators.
3. General Availability (GA): enable self-serve toggle in Console and API with opt-out. Provide migration playbook for customers on Dedicated (how to pin warm pools).
4. Post-GA: analytics-driven tuning for default thresholds and integration with Optimize for automated profile suggestions.

Operational runbook summary (for SRE oncall):
- Symptom: node memory delta grows above 10% and reservoir eviction rate spikes.
  1. Check reservoir controller logs for mass warm events (command: kubectl logs -l app=reservoir-controller).
  2. Force global-evict to relieve pressure: POST /admin/v1/reservoir/evict?mode=global&target=10%
  3. If cross-tenant failures observed, enable temporary per-tenant isolation: toggle per-tenant soft-limit = 0 to pause warming.
  4. Open incident if warm failures > 1% request surface or if route SLOs are breached; assign to owning runtime oncall.

Security & Compliance:
- Reservoir entries inherit tenant encryption policies; snapshots written to disk must be encrypted with tenant KMS keys when persistence is enabled for warm snapshots across restarts.
- Access to admin APIs requires RBAC role 'reservoir-admin' and should be logged with audit events.

Dependencies:
- Serving runtime: KV cache snapshot API and low-latency state serialization (eng-serving-runtime team).
- Quant Advisor service for profile recommendations (applied-ml-and-evals).
- Billing & telemetry pipeline to accept warm-cost line-items (finance-and-legal).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Quality regressions from quantized warms.
  Mitigation: shadow-eval every warmed session against high-fidelity model in the lab and surface regressions to Optimize. Implement per-tenant fallback to full precision if regression > threshold.
- Risk: Warm operations compete for GPU memory and degrade overall throughput.
  Mitigation: conservative default memory budget per-node; emergency global-evict and backpressure signal from runtime to reservoir controller.

Open questions (to resolve before implementation):
- How granular should tenant soft-limits be exposed in Console vs. API? (UI simplicity vs. operational control)
- Should warmed entries be serialized to persistent fast storage (nvme) to survive pod evictions, or only kept in-memory?
- Exact schema for warm-cost attribution that is defensible for billing (per-warm CPU/GPU seconds vs amortized memory cost).

Ownership and timeline:
- Product owner: Aisha Morales (Product Manager)
- Engineering leads: Daniel Park (runtime), Olivia Chen (reservoir controller)
- SLA/telemetry: SRE observability guild
- Target: design & API spec complete by 2026-12-15; engineering MVP complete by 2027-03-01; GA target 2027-05-15.

Related pages and references:
- Runtime architecture & session-kv design: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture/session-kv-design-2026-06-11
- Predictive prefetch scheduler design: /confluence/product-docs/design-specs/predictive-prefetch-and-sticky-session-allocator-design-2026-10-19
- Quant Advisor product brief: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quant-advisor-overview-2026-07-07

Appendix: sample console UX flow (for product/UX):
1) Customer navigates to Route Settings -> Warm State
2) Toggle Warm State: Off | Auto (default) | On (reserved)
3) If Auto: Display recommended tenant budget and projected cost delta ("Estimated warm cost: $12/month at current traffic").
4) Advanced: configure per-tenant warm threshold and eviction policy tune (soft-limit bytes, eviction-preference={age,cost}).

This PRD will be accompanied by a technical API contract document, a design-spec for the reservoir controller, and runbooks for SRE. Feedback requested from reviewers on the eviction heuristics and fidelity tradeoff surface.
